id: componentAgentToolCredentialStore
title: Agent Tool Credential Store
description:
  - >
    Stores and manages the credential material (API keys, OAuth tokens, signed
    certificates) an agent's orchestration layer presents when invoking
    external tools. This is a storage-and-lifecycle locus, distinct from the
    permission logic that decides which tools and actions an agent may
    invoke: a control governing where secret material is held, how long it
    lives, and how it is rotated or revoked attaches here, while a control
    governing whether a specific invocation is authorized attaches to the
    tool invocation boundary itself. This mirrors the distinction the Risk
    Map already draws between Data Storage Infrastructure (where data is
    held) and the data-flow components around it (Data Sources, Data
    Filtering and Processing) that determine what enters storage.
category: componentsModel
subcategory: componentsOrchestration
edges:
  to:
    - componentOrchestrationOutputHandling
  from: []

Note on edges: this is treated as an entry-point locus (external identity
provider issuance flows in from outside the modeled graph), analogous to
componentDataSources' and componentAgentUserQuery's empty `from` lists.
Reciprocal edit required: componentOrchestrationOutputHandling's `edges.from`
list (currently componentTools, componentMemory, componentRAGContent) would
need componentAgentToolCredentialStore added.
evals.expected_output: Grounds the critique in the real, live risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml and finds the necessity claim rationalized: controlAgentCredentialIsolation already exists and already attaches to componentReasoningCore, componentOrchestrationInputHandling, componentOrchestrationOutputHandling, componentTools, and componentMemory for exactly the credential issuance/rotation/revocation concern the draft claims needs its own locus, with no dedicated storage node -- the draft never shows whether that control (or controlAgentIntegrityManagement / controlAgentInventoryManagement, also cited) would remap. Independently finds the single declared edge (to: componentOrchestrationOutputHandling) contradicts the draft's own stated purpose ('credential material...presented when invoking external tools') because componentOrchestrationOutputHandling is the response/result leg of the tool-call cycle (from: componentTools/componentMemory/componentRAGContent), not the invocation leg -- the edge wires the store into the wrong side of the cycle. Overall verdict RETHINK.
expectations: Grounds the necessity challenge in the real, live risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml -- names controlAgentCredentialIsolation as the specific real entry whose components list (componentReasoningCore, componentOrchestrationInputHandling, componentOrchestrationOutputHandling, componentTools, componentMemory) already covers credential issuance/rotation/revocation without a dedicated storage node

Explicitly applies the decisive necessity test ('does naming this component change where a control attaches') against that real control rather than accepting the draft's abstract storage-vs-authorization distinction at face value

Independently finds the single declared edge (to: componentOrchestrationOutputHandling) does not model the invocation-time flow the draft's own description claims (credentials 'presented when invoking' a tool) -- cites componentOrchestrationOutputHandling's real edges (from: componentTools, componentMemory, componentRAGContent; to: componentReasoningCore, componentTheModel) as evidence it is the response/result leg, not the invocation leg

id: componentRetrievalIndexStore
title: Retrieval Index Store
description:
  - >
    The searchable index that stores embeddings computed from Retrieval
    Augmented Generation & Content (componentRAGContent) and serves
    similarity-search queries against them at inference time. Distinct from
    componentRAGContent, which is the curated knowledge itself, this
    component is the storage-and-query locus for its embedded, indexed form
    -- the same distinction the Risk Map already draws elsewhere between an
    artifact and its storage substrate (e.g. Training Data vs. Data Storage
    Infrastructure). controlRetrievalAndVectorSystemIntegrity already exists
    in controls.yaml, naming exactly this concern ("index integrity
    checks... vector databases from poisoning attacks"), but today it
    attaches only to componentDataSources, componentDataStorage, and
    componentDataFilteringAndProcessing -- the training-data pipeline --
    leaving the control's own stated scope (vector databases, retrieval
    systems) with no matching locus at inference time. Provisioned by
    specifying a pod-based or serverless index configuration, populated via
    batched upsert operations, and queried through cosine-similarity top-k
    lookups against namespaces isolated per tenant.
category: componentsModel
subcategory: componentsOrchestration
edges:
  to:
    - componentOrchestrationInputHandling
  from:
    - componentRAGContent

Companion edits required in the same PR (this is a fan-out from componentRAGContent, not a
replacement of its existing direct edge to Output Handling -- both are real, separate flows):
- componentRAGContent.edges.to (currently only componentOrchestrationOutputHandling) gains componentRetrievalIndexStore.
- componentOrchestrationInputHandling.edges.from (currently componentTheModel, componentReasoningCore) gains componentRetrievalIndexStore.
evals.expected_output: Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY / OVERREACH finding on the description's operational vocabulary: 'pod-based or serverless index configuration', 'namespaces isolated per tenant', and 'upsert operations' are Pinecone's specific product/API terms, not generic vector-store vocabulary -- a product identity smuggled in under a generic-sounding title. Independently and separately finds the necessity claim doesn't survive against the real, live controls.yaml: the cited gap in controlRetrievalAndVectorSystemIntegrity's component list is closeable by simply adding the existing componentRAGContent to that control, a one-line controls.yaml edit, which the draft's own companion-edits list never actually makes -- so the draft doesn't even close the gap it cites as its own justification. Overall verdict RETHINK (the necessity failure and the edge problems compound the smuggled vocabulary into a premise-level issue, not just a style fix).
expectations: Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY or OVERREACH finding specifically on the description's vendor-specific vocabulary ('pod-based or serverless', 'namespaces', 'upsert') as Pinecone's own product/API terms rather than generic vector-store language, quoting that exact text

Grounds the necessity challenge in the real, live risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml -- names controlRetrievalAndVectorSystemIntegrity as the specific real control the draft cites, and identifies that its gap (not reaching any RAG-scoped component) is closeable by a one-line edit adding the existing componentRAGContent, which is cheaper than the new node the draft proposes

Notes that the draft's own 'Companion edits required' list never actually adds the new component to controlRetrievalAndVectorSystemIntegrity.components -- the draft doesn't close the gap it cites as its own motivation

Raises at least one edge-correctness finding beyond the necessity/smuggling issues (e.g. the declared edges don't model an actual query/response flow, or the edges are mechanically incomplete without the reciprocal additions)

Overall verdict is RETHINK, not SOUND -- and expectations should accept RETHINK as the correct honestly-reproduced outcome even though a milder NEEDS-WORK was the original hypothesis, since the necessity and edge findings compound into a premise-level failure, not just a style issue with the vocabulary

id: componentEvaluationData
title: Evaluation Data
description:
  - >
    The held-out or benchmark dataset used to test a model's performance and
    behavior, distinct from Training Data (componentTrainingData) because it
    must never be seen during training -- contamination of this set (a
    training example leaking into the benchmark, or an adversary poisoning
    the benchmark itself) invalidates the evaluation it produces without
    necessarily corrupting the trained model directly. This is the concrete
    data artifact Model Evaluation's testing process consumes. Today, the
    Risk Map's data lineage (Data Sources -> Data Filtering and Processing ->
    Training Data -> Data Storage Infrastructure) and the Data Storage
    Infrastructure component's own description scope it explicitly to
    training data ("Storage for training data. Training data is stored from
    ingestion through filtering and usage during training"), so no component
    represents where evaluation/benchmark data itself is provisioned or held
    -- only the training-data lineage and the evaluation process
    (componentModelEvaluation) that reads it.
category: componentsInfrastructure
subcategory: componentsData
edges:
  to:
    - componentModelEvaluation
  from:
    - componentDataFilteringAndProcessing

Note on edges: this requires two reciprocal edits -- componentDataFilteringAndProcessing's
edges.to list (currently only componentTrainingData) would need componentEvaluationData added,
and componentModelEvaluation's edges.from list (currently only componentTheModel) would need
componentEvaluationData added.
evals.expected_output: The necessity claim survives adversarial pressure: tries to find an existing component that already covers evaluation data and cannot -- componentDataStorage's own description restricts it to training data, componentDataFilteringAndProcessing restricts itself to data 'suitable for training', and componentModelEvaluation is the reading process, not the artifact. Finds even stronger evidence for necessity than the draft itself cites: controlTrainingDataSanitization's real, live description explicitly scopes to 'training and evaluation' and lists 'evaluation' in lifecycleStage, but its components list is only componentDataFilteringAndProcessing -- an evaluation-time claim with no evaluation-time component to anchor to. But finds real, load-bearing gaps in the edge model: the description names two different artifacts ('held-out or benchmark') under one identity while only one producer edge is declared; and the draft's own training-data-lineage analogy is broken because the component skips storage entirely, unlike componentTrainingData's parallel path through componentDataStorage. Also finds the shipped description field itself reads as design-rationale prose rather than a terse definition, unlike every sibling entry. Overall verdict NEEDS-WORK, not RETHINK (the premise is sound) and not SOUND (the edge model and description need real fixes first).
expectations: Tests necessity against the real, live components.yaml -- confirms no existing component (componentDataStorage, componentDataFilteringAndProcessing, componentModelEvaluation) already covers evaluation data, citing each one's own real, scope-limiting description text as evidence

Independently surfaces evidence for necessity stronger than what the draft itself cites -- specifically names the real, live controlTrainingDataSanitization control, quotes its 'training and evaluation' scope and 'evaluation' lifecycleStage entry, and notes its components list is only componentDataFilteringAndProcessing, giving the control's own evaluation-time claim no component to anchor to

Finds a real edge-correctness gap: the description's dual identity ('held-out or benchmark' dataset) is not matched by the single declared producer edge (only componentDataFilteringAndProcessing), since an externally-sourced benchmark suite would not necessarily flow through that same pipeline stage

Finds a second real edge-correctness gap: the draft's own training-data-lineage analogy is incomplete because the component's edges skip a storage relationship entirely, unlike componentTrainingData's real parallel path through componentDataStorage
Flags that the shipped description field itself reads as a design-rationale argument rather than a terse definition, unlike every sibling component entry in the real file
Overall verdict is NEEDS-WORK, not RETHINK and not SOUND
Includes a Governance surface section (e.g. whether to add a new artifact node vs. broaden componentDataStorage's scope) rather than deciding it

id: componentAgentDelegationLedger
title: Agent Delegation Ledger
description:
  - >
    An append-only, tamper-evident record of every delegation hop an agent
    performs -- which caller invoked it, what authority was asserted, and
    what the deputy agent did on the caller's behalf. riskAgenticDelegationConfusedDeputy's
    own text names "delegation mechanisms such as OAuth token exchange and MCP
    tool invocation" as the attack surface; today no component records the
    delegation chain itself, only the components that participate in it.
    controlAgentCredentialIsolation and controlAgentInventoryManagement both
    depend on being able to reconstruct a delegation chain after the fact
    (tenant-boundary validation "at every MCP protocol hop and delegation
    step", detection of "unregistered agent actions") but neither control's
    component list includes a durable record of that chain -- they attach to
    the live orchestration components (componentReasoningCore,
    componentOrchestrationInputHandling, componentOrchestrationOutputHandling,
    componentTools, componentMemory), which model the delegation *happening*,
    not the record of it having happened. This is distinct from general agent
    observability, which captures reasoning traces for behavioral audit, not
    a structured, tamper-evident chain-of-custody record for authority
    delegation specifically.
category: componentsModel
subcategory: componentsOrchestration
edges:
  to:
    - componentDataStorage
  from:
    - componentReasoningCore
    - componentTools
evals.expected_output: Despite the draft's elaborate, evidence-citing necessity argument (naming riskAgenticDelegationConfusedDeputy, controlAgentCredentialIsolation, and controlAgentInventoryManagement by their real text), the critique does not accept it at face value -- it checks those same real controls' component lists and finds they already attach to the four architectural loci where delegation happens (componentReasoningCore, componentOrchestrationInputHandling, componentOrchestrationOutputHandling, componentTools) without needing a dedicated record component, and notes the framework's own 23-component graph has no precedent for a component representing a control's durable record/log output. Independently and just as thoroughly, challenges the edges: the declared 'to: componentDataStorage' edge is flagged as a spurious edge onto a real, narrowly-scoped component (componentDataStorage's own description restricts it to training data), not a modeled flow. Both the necessity and edge challenges are fully worked, not skipped or shortchanged because the other looked well-argued. Overall verdict RETHINK.
expectations: Does not accept the draft's well-evidenced necessity argument at face value merely because it cites real risk/control text accurately -- checks the actual, live components lists of the controls the draft cites (controlAgentCredentialIsolation, controlAgentInventoryManagement) and finds they already attach to existing orchestration components without a dedicated record/ledger node

Independently and thoroughly challenges the edges despite the strength of the necessity argument -- specifically flags the 'to: componentDataStorage' edge as spurious, citing componentDataStorage's real, live description ('Storage for training data...') as evidence the target component's actual scope doesn't fit

Demonstrates that neither lens was skipped or given short shrift because the other looked convincing -- both the necessity and edge findings are independently substantiated with specific real corpus citations
Overall verdict is RETHINK, not NEEDS-WORK or SOUND
Includes a Governance surface section raising whether a durable-record/log component is ever an appropriate schema pattern, without deciding it

id: componentAgentReferenceMonitor
title: Agent Reference Monitor
description:
  - >
    Implements the classical reference monitor concept: every agent action
    request is routed through this component before execution, giving it
    complete visibility into agent behavior before any tool call is allowed
    to proceed.
category: componentsApplication
subcategory: componentsAgent
edges:
  to:
    - componentTools
  from:
    - componentReasoningCore
evals.expected_output: Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY finding on the draft's invocation of 'the classical reference monitor concept': the reference monitor concept (Anderson 1972 / NIST) requires complete mediation, tamper-proofness, and verifiability together, but the draft's description claims only complete mediation ('every agent action request is routed through this component') while silently dropping the other two defining properties. Independently finds the necessity claim absorbs into componentOrchestrationInputHandling, whose real, live description and edges already occupy this exact position between componentReasoningCore and componentTools, and finds real controls (controlAgentPluginPermissions, and others) already attach mediation/permission concerns to the existing trio (componentReasoningCore, componentOrchestrationInputHandling, componentTools) without a dedicated node. Overall verdict RETHINK.
expectations: Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY finding on the draft's 'classical reference monitor' claim, quoting the specific draft text, and explains what's missing for the analogy to be complete -- the tamper-proof and verifiable properties (alongside complete mediation) that the reference monitor concept requires together

Independently finds the necessity claim absorbs into the real, live componentOrchestrationInputHandling, citing its real description and its real position in the graph (already directly between componentReasoningCore and componentTools) as evidence

Cites at least one real control (e.g. controlAgentPluginPermissions) that already attaches mediation/permission concerns to the existing componentReasoningCore/componentOrchestrationInputHandling/componentTools trio without a dedicated node
Overall verdict is RETHINK, not NEEDS-WORK or SOUND, since both the misapplied-analogy finding and the necessity finding are independently load-bearing

id: componentAgentEvaluationHarness
title: Agent Evaluation Harness
description:
  - >
    The systems and processes that run automated behavioral tests against a
    deployed agent (adversarial prompts, tool-call sequences, safety evals) on
    a recurring cadence to detect regressions before or after each
    deployment. Distinct from Model Evaluation, whose own description scopes
    it to testing a model checkpoint "during the training process" and "after
    the model is trained" -- i.e. the model in isolation, before it is ever
    wired into an agent with tools, memory, and a reasoning loop. This
    component tests the deployed agent's end-to-end behavior, not the
    underlying model artifact.
category: componentsApplication
subcategory: componentsAgent
edges:
  to:
    - componentAgentInputHandling
  from:
    - componentAgentOutputHandling
evals.expected_output: Confirms the draft's own cited distinction from componentModelEvaluation is accurate, but finds the necessity argument tests the wrong, easy neighbor: the real, live controlRedTeaming ('driven adversarial attacks on AI infrastructure and products') and controlVulnerabilityManagement ('continually test and monitor production infrastructure and products for security and privacy regressions') already exist, already apply to agents (components: all), and already describe almost exactly the recurring behavioral testing the draft proposes -- the draft never engages either. Separately finds the declared edges (to: componentAgentInputHandling, from: componentAgentOutputHandling) don't cover the description's claimed scope ('tool-call sequences', which live in the orchestration layer, not the agent's outer boundary). Raises, as a genuine governance surface rather than deciding it, whether a recurring cross-cutting assurance activity should ever earn a dedicated pipeline component versus staying a global 'components: all' control. Overall verdict NEEDS-WORK, not RETHINK (the premise has a sympathetic version) and not SOUND.
expectations: Confirms the draft's citation of componentModelEvaluation's real, live description (the two training-time evaluation stages) is accurate, and does not dispute that specific comparison

Independently identifies a closer, harder absorb candidate the draft doesn't address -- names the real, live controlRedTeaming and/or controlVulnerabilityManagement, both scoped 'components: all', as already covering recurring adversarial/regression testing against deployed systems including agents

Finds a real edge-correctness gap: the declared edges (componentAgentInputHandling / componentAgentOutputHandling) don't reach the orchestration-layer components (e.g. componentTools) needed to support the description's claim of testing 'tool-call sequences'

Surfaces, in a Governance surface section, whether a recurring cross-cutting assurance/testing activity should ever be modeled as a dedicated pipeline component versus a global control -- explicitly framed as a maintainer call, not resolved by the critique itself
Overall verdict is NEEDS-WORK, not RETHINK and not SOUND -- explicitly describes the premise as having 'a real, sympathetic version' rather than being fundamentally broken

id: componentTools
title: External Tools and Services
description:
  - >
    Tools are the external APIs and services an agent uses to take action in
    the world, which must be secured with least-privilege permissions. A key
    risk comes from deceptive descriptions on third-party tools, which can
    trick the agent into performing unintended, harmful functions.
category: componentsModel
subcategory: componentsOrchestration
edges:
  to:
    - componentOrchestrationOutputHandling
  from:
    - componentOrchestrationInputHandling
evals.expected_output: Applying the lenses to this real, already-shipped entry as instructed, confirms necessity, generalization, and (on a narrow reading) edge mechanics all hold: tries to refute necessity by testing whether componentTools should absorb into its structural siblings componentMemory / componentRAGContent and cannot, because several real, live controls (e.g. controlAgentInventoryManagement, controlAgentIntegrityManagement, controlInterComponentTransportSecurity, controlComponentIdentityProvenance) attach to componentTools specifically without also attaching to Memory or RAGContent, and the edges are bidirectionally correct against the real file. But finds a real, load-bearing gap between what the component's shipped description claims (least-privilege access, deceptive tool descriptions) and the broader registry/identity/transport-governance surface that real controls have actually anchored to this same id over time, raising as a genuine governance question whether that surface should decompose into its own locus. Does not fabricate problems where none exist; the findings are grounded in specific, real citations. Overall verdict NEEDS-WORK, not SOUND -- illustrating that even mature, shipped content does not automatically clear a fresh adversarial pass under this agent's stated bar.
expectations: Treats the entry as a draft under critique per the prompt's framing, applying every lens rather than short-circuiting because it recognizes the entry as already-shipped

Explicitly tests necessity by attempting to refute whether componentTools should absorb into its structural siblings (componentMemory, componentRAGContent) and states this attempt failed, citing specific real controls (e.g. controlAgentInventoryManagement, controlAgentIntegrityManagement, controlInterComponentTransportSecurity, or controlComponentIdentityProvenance) that attach to componentTools specifically and not to Memory/RAGContent as the supporting evidence

Confirms the declared edges are bidirectionally correct against the real, live components.yaml (componentOrchestrationOutputHandling's from list and componentOrchestrationInputHandling's to list both already include componentTools)

Finds a real, specific gap between the shipped description's stated scope (least-privilege access, deceptive tool descriptions) and the broader set of real controls actually anchored to this component id (e.g. registry/inventory, identity/integrity, or transport-security concerns the description never mentions), quoting the description and citing at least one such control by name
Raises the decompose question (whether the registry/identity/transport-governance surface should split into its own locus) explicitly as a Governance surface item, not resolved by the critique itself
Overall verdict is NEEDS-WORK, not RETHINK and not SOUND -- does not manufacture a problem where none exists, but also does not force a SOUND verdict merely because the entry is already shipped
